# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yang_2021_metformin_ddi_pbpk"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yang_2021_metformin_ddi_pbpk"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics13050698> (open access, PMC8151202)
* Supplement: Table S1 (physiology), Table S2 (tissue:plasma ratios), Table S3/S4
  (observed/predicted metformin dose ranging), Table S5 (perpetrator PK) and
  Table S6 (DDI schedules).

Yang and colleagues built a whole-body PBPK model for metformin in which
disposition is controlled by the organic-cation transporters OCT1 (hepatic),
OCT2 (renal), OCT3 (intestinal), the plasma-membrane monoamine transporter
PMAT (intestinal) and the multidrug/toxin extrusion transporters MATE1/2-K
(renal). Intestinal absorption is nonlinear, driven by Michaelis-Menten uptake
through OCT3 and PMAT. The model predicts the interaction of metformin with six
perpetrators that competitively inhibit these carriers: cimetidine,
pyrimethamine, trimethoprim, ondansetron, rabeprazole and verapamil.

This is the same China Pharmaceutical University group, and the same Table S1
human physiology, as `Kong_2020_vonoprazan_human_pbpk`.

# How the parameterised perpetrator slot works

The paper solves metformin together with one perpetrator at a time. The model
carries that as two coupled blocks of states:

* the **metformin** block (bare state names, output `Cc`): the victim, always
  the full transporter-resolved whole-body model;
* the **perpetrator** block (`_perpetrator` suffix, output `Cperp`): a
  parameterised slot that ships set to cimetidine and whose values are swapped
  for any of the six perpetrators from the model's `drugLibrary` metadata.

The perpetrator inhibits the four metformin carriers competitively, each term
of the form `1 / (1 + fub_perp * C_perp / Ki)`. Dosing the perpetrator states
with nothing recovers the metformin-alone (control) arm, so one model object
gives both arms of each interaction.

Cimetidine uses the same transporter-resolved liver (hepatic blood +
hepatocytes) and kidney (renal blood + tubule) structure as metformin
(`p_tr = 1`); the other five perpetrators are described by a well-stirred
liver and kidney (`p_tr = 0`). Both structures are present in every solve and
the inactive one is held at zero by the `p_tr` / `1 - p_tr` multipliers. This
follows the parameterised-perpetrator design of
`CherkaouiRbati_2017_midazolam_qsp` and `Stader_2021_bictegravir_ddi_pbpk`.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Yang_2021_metformin_ddi_pbpk")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
lib <- ui$meta$drugLibrary

perps <- c("cimetidine", "pyrimethamine", "trimethoprim", "ondansetron", "rabeprazole", "verapamil")

# Load a drugLibrary column into a named parameter vector for rxSolve.
perp_params <- function(drug) stats::setNames(lib[[drug]], lib$parameter)

# Solve metformin +/- a perpetrator. Doses in mg (converted to ug); times in
# minutes. A zero perpetrator dose is the control arm.
solve_run <- function(drug, met_mg, met_t = 0, perp_mg = 0, perp_t = 0, tend_min = 24 * 60) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = met_mg * 1000, cmt = "stomach", time = met_t)
  if (perp_mg > 0) {
    ev <- ev |> rxode2::et(amt = perp_mg * 1000, cmt = "stomach_perpetrator", time = perp_t)
  }
  ev <- ev |> rxode2::et(seq(0, met_t + tend_min, by = 2))
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, perp_params(drug), ev, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10))
  s[s$time >= met_t, ]
}

# Trapezoidal AUC of Cc over the window, minutes -> hours.
trap_auc <- function(time, conc) sum(diff(time) * (head(conc, -1) + tail(conc, -1)) / 2) / 60
```

# Population

A PBPK model has no fitted population. The transporter and metabolism
parameters came from in vitro data and prior models (Table 1), the physiology
from Table S1 (a 70-kg adult), and the tissue:plasma ratios from Table S2. The
clinical plasma data used for comparison came from healthy-volunteer studies.
The paper's visual predictive check estimated inter-individual variances on
Vmax,OCT3, the hepatic OCT1, renal OCT2 and renal MATE clearances, and the
gastrointestinal transit rate, but did not report them, so this model is
typical-value only (no random effects). The same information is available from
`readModelDb("Yang_2021_metformin_ddi_pbpk")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries a comment giving the table or equation it comes
from. The `drugLibrary` metadata holds the per-perpetrator inputs (Table 1 drug
parameters and Table S2 tissue:blood ratios); molecular weights are from
PubChem. A column loaded into the `p_*` / `ki_*_um` / `kp_p` parameters
reproduces that perpetrator.

```{r source-trace-drugs}
lib |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = paste(
      "Per-perpetrator inputs of the parameterised perpetrator slot",
      "(drugLibrary metadata). Units are those of the corresponding ini() labels."
    ),
    digits = 5
  )
```

```{r source-trace-equations}
tibble::tribble(
  ~Component, ~Source,
  "Gut lumen / wall transit, 6 segments", "Eqs 1-3; Table S1 transit constants",
  "Metformin OCT3 + PMAT M-M absorption", "Eqs 2-3; Table 1 / Methods Vmax, Km, PBSF, Tsf",
  "Hepatic OCT1 uptake + passive diffusion + metabolism", "Eqs 7-8; Table 1",
  "Renal OCT2 uptake/back-flux, MATE efflux, GFR", "Eqs 12-13; Table 1",
  "Competitive inhibition at OCT1/OCT2/OCT3/MATE", "Eqs 4, 7-8, 12-13; Table 1 Ki",
  "Perpetrator well-stirred liver / kidney (tr = 0)", "Eqs 11, 14-15",
  "Whole-body blood and tissue mass balance", "Eqs 16-17; Table S1",
  "Tissue:blood partition ratios", "Table S2 (Kp / Rb)"
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Source location for each model component.")
```

# Metformin nonlinear absorption (Table S4)

The paper's headline absorption result is that metformin oral clearance
(dose/AUC) rises with dose because intestinal OCT3/PMAT uptake saturates. The
model reproduces the predicted dose-ranging Cmax and AUC of Table S4.

```{r dose-ranging}
doses <- c(250, 500, 750, 850, 1000)
sim_conc <- bind_rows(lapply(doses, function(d) {
  s <- solve_run("cimetidine", met_mg = d, perp_mg = 0)
  data.frame(treatment = paste(d, "mg"), dose = d, time = s$time / 60, Cc = s$Cc)
}))

# PKNCA single-dose NCA, grouped by dose. One id per dose arm.
nca_conc <- sim_conc |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(id = dose) |>
  select(id, treatment, dose, time, Cc)
nca_dose <- data.frame(id = doses, treatment = paste(doses, "mg"), dose = doses, time = 0)
met_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, dose ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
```

```{r dose-ranging-compare}
sim_wide <- as.data.frame(met_nca) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
# Table S4 predicted values (the model's own target).
tableS4 <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = paste(doses, "mg"),
  cmax = c(0.67, 0.95, 1.22, 1.32, 1.47),
  auclast = c(4.80, 7.68, 10.19, 11.15, 12.55)
)
met_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_wide, tableS4,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "auclast"),
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", auclast = "h*ug/mL")
)
knitr::kable(
  met_cmp,
  caption = "Metformin dose ranging: PKNCA of the simulation vs Table S4 predictions. * > 20% difference."
)
# Structural gate: the as-run model must reproduce Table S4 to a few percent.
met_diff <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.eE-]", "", met_cmp[["% diff"]]))
stopifnot(all(abs(met_diff) < 3))
```

```{r dose-ranging-plot, fig.cap = "Metformin plasma concentration by oral dose (replicates Figure 3a of Yang 2021)."}
ggplot(sim_conc, aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Metformin plasma (ug/mL)", colour = "Dose (mg)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Transporter contributions to metformin exposure (Figure 6b)

The individual contribution of each transporter is the percent change in
metformin AUC when that transporter is removed. The model reproduces the Figure
6b values: renal OCT2 and MATE dominate (each roughly +160% when removed),
intestinal OCT3 and PMAT act in the opposite direction, and hepatic OCT1 is
minor.

```{r contributions}
auc250 <- function(over = NULL) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 250 * 1000, cmt = "stomach") |> rxode2::et(seq(0, 24 * 60, by = 2))
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, if (is.null(over)) numeric(0) else over, ev, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10))
  trap_auc(s$time, s$Cc)
}
ctrl <- auc250()
ko <- c(OCT3 = "vmax_oct3", PMAT = "vmax_pmat", OCT1 = "clint_up_oct1", OCT2 = "clint_up_oct2", MATE = "clint_eff_mate")
paper_pct <- c(OCT3 = -35.94, PMAT = -12.06, OCT1 = 15.67, OCT2 = 160.30, MATE = 159.80)
contrib <- data.frame(
  Transporter = names(ko),
  `Simulated %` = round(sapply(ko, function(p) 100 * (auc250(stats::setNames(0, p)) / ctrl - 1)), 2),
  `Paper %` = paper_pct,
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(contrib, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Contribution of each transporter to metformin AUC (Figure 6b).")
# Deterministic structural gate: each contribution reproduces Figure 6b to <1%.
stopifnot(all(abs(contrib[["Simulated %"]] - contrib[["Paper %"]]) < 1))
```

# Perpetrator standalone pharmacokinetics (Table 2)

Each perpetrator's own plasma PK is reproduced by loading its `drugLibrary`
column and dosing only the perpetrator slot.

```{r perp-standalone}
perp_doses <- list(cimetidine = 400, pyrimethamine = 50, trimethoprim = 210, ondansetron = 8, rabeprazole = 40, verapamil = 40)
perp_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(names(perp_doses), function(d) {
  dose <- perp_doses[[d]]
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose * 1000, cmt = "stomach_perpetrator") |> rxode2::et(seq(0, 24 * 60, by = 2))
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, perp_params(d), ev, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10))
  data.frame(Perpetrator = d, `Dose (mg)` = dose, Cmax = max(s$Cperp), `AUC0-24` = trap_auc(s$time, s$Cperp), check.names = FALSE)
}))
# Paper Table 2 predicted Cmax / AUC (same doses).
perp_tbl$`Paper Cmax` <- c(2.06, 0.57, 2.18, 0.046, 0.40, 0.050)
perp_tbl$`Paper AUC` <- c(9.17, 31.18, 28.26, 0.203, 1.27, 0.28)
knitr::kable(perp_tbl, digits = 3, caption = "Perpetrator standalone Cmax (ug/mL) and AUC0-24 (ug*h/mL) vs Table 2 predictions.")
```

# Drug-drug interactions with metformin (Table 3)

Loading a perpetrator and dosing both drugs on the Table S6 schedule gives the
interaction. The interaction ratio is AUC (or Cmax) with perpetrator over the
metformin-alone control.

```{r ddi}
# perpetrator, metformin dose (mg), metformin time offset (min), perpetrator dose (mg)
ddi_cases <- tibble::tribble(
  ~perp,            ~met_mg, ~met_t, ~perp_mg,
  "cimetidine",     500,     120,    400,
  "pyrimethamine",  500,     0,      50,
  "ondansetron",    850,     60,     8,
  "verapamil",      750,     0,      180,
  "rabeprazole",    500,     720,    20
)
ddi <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ddi_cases)), function(i) {
  r <- ddi_cases[i, ]
  a <- solve_run(r$perp, r$met_mg, r$met_t, 0)
  b <- solve_run(r$perp, r$met_mg, r$met_t, r$perp_mg, 0)
  data.frame(
    Perpetrator = r$perp,
    `AUCR (sim)` = round(trap_auc(b$time, b$Cc) / trap_auc(a$time, a$Cc), 2),
    `CmaxR (sim)` = round(max(b$Cc) / max(a$Cc), 2),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
# Paper Table 3 AUCR / CmaxR for the matched rows.
ddi$`AUCR (paper)` <- c(1.52, 2.09, 1.16, 1.09, 1.00)
ddi$`CmaxR (paper)` <- c(1.40, 1.73, 1.16, 1.05, 0.95)
knitr::kable(ddi, caption = "Metformin interaction ratios vs Table 3. See the deviations section for cimetidine and pyrimethamine.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations (Errata)

The model is an as-run reproduction of the published WinNonlin model, and
several values deviate from the printed equations and constants. Each is
documented inline in the model file and summarised here.

* **Metformin OCT3/PMAT absorption (Table 1 constants).** The model reproduces
  Table S4 only when (i) the Michaelis-Menten uptake is driven by the gut-lumen
  concentration `A_i / V_i` rather than the enterocyte concentration of the
  printed Eqs 2-3 (taken literally, the printed form drives the lumen negative
  and makes absorption linear), and (ii) the reported Km (2.46 and 1.68 mM) and
  Vmax (12.08 and 15.28 nmol/mg/min, used as /1000) are applied to the ug
  amounts without molar-to-mass conversion. This dimensionally inconsistent
  as-run form reproduces Table S4 at every dose, the oral microdose and the
  OCT3/PMAT knockouts; the dimensionally correct form predicts a Cmax four to
  six times too high. The maintainers ship the as-run form that reproduces the
  paper.
* **Hepatic passive-diffusion clearance CLint,pd.** Eqs 7-8 use a
  hepatocyte-to-blood passive-diffusion clearance that is printed nowhere in
  the paper or supplement. Six independent printed metformin outputs (the
  control AUC, the no-OCT1 and no-OCT2 percentages, the no-OCT2 AUC, and the
  500 and 1000 mg AUCs) all back-solve to a value between 10 and 12 mL/min, so
  the maintainers ship 11 mL/min. Cimetidine is insensitive to its own
  hepatic passive diffusion, so the perpetrator value is 0.
* **Rabeprazole metabolic clearance.** The printed `fub * CLint` form (fub 0.04,
  CLint 955.6 mL/min) over-predicts rabeprazole exposure about 17-fold. The
  published rabeprazole PK is reproduced when CLint is applied as a blood
  clearance without `fub`; the model encodes this for rabeprazole only by
  shipping `p_clmet = 955.6 / 0.04 = 23890`, so the model's `fub * CLint` term
  recovers 955.6 mL/min.
* **Cimetidine interaction is under-predicted.** With the printed
  transporter-resolved cimetidine structure the model gives an interaction of
  about AUCR 1.11 / CmaxR 1.10, against the published 1.52 / 1.40. A
  well-stirred cimetidine reproduces the interaction but then over-predicts
  cimetidine's own exposure about two-fold, so neither structure reproduces
  both. The maintainers follow the Methods text and keep the printed
  transporter structure, and note the interaction shortfall here.
* **Pyrimethamine interaction.** Pyrimethamine's own exposure is poorly
  predicted by the paper (Table 2 predicted AUC 31-47 vs observed 42-124), and
  its interaction ratio is correspondingly approximate.
* **Printed-equation typos, corrected by mass balance.** Eq 7 as printed has an
  `A_h,b / V_h,c` term (should be `V_h,b`) and multiplies a portal inflow by
  `Kg:b` rather than dividing; Eq 11 has a hepatic outflow without the `Kh:b`
  partition. The model uses the mass-balance-consistent forms.
* **No inter-individual variability.** The paper's VPC estimated variances but
  did not report them, so the model is typical-value only.
* **Molecular weights** used for the Ki unit conversion (uM to ug/mL) are from
  PubChem, not the paper.
